population_one_line: Adult Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, single tertiary center, Zaragoza Spain (Mar 2020-Feb 2021)
ttp_reported: Mean TTP 16h (SD 17); cutpoint TTP <=12h vs >12h; 17% had TTP <=12h
outcome_one_line: TTP <=12h associated with sepsis OR 2.6 (1.1-6.2); trend with 14-day mortality (TTP 2.5h vs 10h, p=0.07); 14-day mortality 24.2%, 30-day 40%
notes: Spanish article with English abstract. Reports TTP categorical and continuous comparisons with sepsis and mortality.

population_one_line: Patients with Candida BSI at single US tertiary center over 2 years; mixed adult/pediatric
ttp_reported: Mean TTP by species: C. albicans 35.3+/-18.1h, C. glabrata 80.0+/-22.4h
outcome_one_line: Mean time to appropriate therapy in nonsurvivors 58.6+/-40.0h vs survivors 61.3h (p=0.81); no formal TTP-mortality model
notes: Primarily a microbiology/TTP-by-species descriptive paper. Single t-test of time-to-appropriate-therapy by survival; not a TTP-outcome quantitative association meeting criteria. Time to appropriate therapy not TTP per se.

population_one_line: CoNS-positive blood cultures in tertiary care hospital (Murcia, Spain), Jan-Jun 2010
ttp_reported: TTP <16h tested as predictor of true bacteremia (OR 5.688, 95% CI 2.030-15.933)
outcome_one_line: Outcome is true bacteremia vs contamination (diagnostic, not clinical outcome)
notes: Conference abstract (ECCMID 2011 P1474). Outcome is microbiologic classification (true bacteremia vs contamination), not a clinical outcome (mortality, persistent bacteremia, etc.). Also wrong design (abstract).

population_one_line: Adult inpatients with S. aureus bacteremia >=3 days, Mayo Clinic 2006-2011
ttp_reported: Not reported - study focuses on duration of bacteremia and 'skip phenomenon' (intermittent negative cultures)
outcome_one_line: Predictors of skip phenomenon - no TTP analysis
notes: IDWeek 2016 conference oral abstract. Concerns duration of bacteremia and skip phenomenon, not TTP. No TTP-outcome association reported.

population_one_line: Patients with suspected infective endocarditis, single French hospital 2016-2019 (194 with positive BC for IE)
ttp_reported: TTP medians reported by pathogen group (e.g., S. aureus 13.4h aerobic, 18.95h anaerobic)
outcome_one_line: No TTP-clinical outcome analysis; focus is on utility of prolonged incubation beyond 5 days
notes: Study aim is whether prolonged incubation (>5d) helps IE diagnosis. TTP described per pathogen but not analyzed vs any clinical outcome (mortality, relapse, etc.).

population_one_line: Adult leukemia inpatients with S. epidermidis BSI treated empirically with linezolid, MD Anderson 2012-2015
outcome_one_line: Linezolid-resistant vs susceptible S. epidermidis adverse outcomes; persistent bacteremia 36.4% vs 8.2% (aRR 5.2)
notes: IDWeek 2016 conference oral abstract. No TTP analyzed. Exposure is linezolid resistance, not TTP.

population_one_line: Persistent MRSA infections, Singapore General Hospital 2005-2006; 10 hVISA/VISA cases vs 30 VS-MRSA controls
ttp_reported: Not reported (reports duration of culture positivity/bacteremia, not TTP)
outcome_one_line: hVISA/VISA vs VS-MRSA: longer bacteremia duration, no mortality difference
notes: Compares 'duration of culture positivity' (length of bacteremia in days) - this is bacteremia duration, NOT time to first blood culture positivity (TTP). No TTP analyzed.

population_one_line: Medical and surgical patients with midline catheters, monocentric French prospective study (per title)
outcome_one_line: Risk of midline catheter-related bloodstream infection (incidence study)
notes: Extracted text file (127 lines) contains only an unrelated vascular access conference proceedings, not the Fournier full paper. Based on title, study focuses on incidence/risk of midline-catheter BSI, not TTP-outcome association. Excluded as no TTP analysis indicated by title/scope.

population_one_line: Adults with CoNS blood cultures, St Luke's Tokyo 2004-2017
ttp_reported: TTP categorical (<24h, 24-48h, >48h) as predictor of true infection
outcome_one_line: TTP <24h aOR 4.83 (2.68-8.68), 24-48h aOR 1.93 (1.11-3.36) for true CoNS infection vs contamination
notes: IDWeek 2018 poster abstract (conference). Outcome is diagnostic classification (true infection vs contamination), not clinical outcome (mortality, relapse, etc.). Excluded for wrong_design and wrong outcome type.

population_one_line: Acute brucellosis cases, single Saudi hospital 2016-2019 (62 bacteremic, 84 non-bacteremic)
ttp_reported: Median time to detect Brucella in BC 3d (IQR 2-3), all within 3d
outcome_one_line: Bacteremia (yes/no) vs chronic brucellosis OR 7.25 (1.41-37.23); no TTP-outcome analysis
notes: Exposure analyzed is bacteremia status (positive vs negative blood culture), not TTP. TTP described descriptively only; no TTP-outcome quantitative association.
